slides.title: FM-VLA: Force-based Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models in Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: FORCE-BASED MEMORY FOR CONTACT-RICH ROBOTIC MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: FM-VLA introduces force-based memory tokens using a pretrained VAE to help vision-language-action models reason about temporal context in contact-rich tasks. This approach outperforms vision-only memory in visually ambiguous scenarios with minimal inference overhead.

card.one_liner: FM-VLA uses force-based memory to enable temporal reasoning for non-Markovian, contact-rich robotic manipulation tasks.
card.key_idea: A pretrained VAE compresses long-horizon wrench histories into compact memory tokens, combined with short-term state history to condition a flow-matching VLA action expert.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on three bimanual tasks (finding blocks, pressing buttons, wiping dishes); achieved 83.3% average success rate, significantly outperforming memoryless and vision-memory baselines.
card.limitation: The fixed 8-token VAE bottleneck may be insufficient for very long-horizon tasks requiring memory of hundreds of contact events.

slides.title: Towards Artificial Nerves: Biomimetic Optical-Fiber Tactile Sensing for Robots
slides.highlight: OptiTac emulates human mechanoreceptor architecture using optical fibers to enable high-resolution, interpretable tactile sensing for dexterous robotic manipulation.

card.one_liner: OptiTac is a biomimetic tactile sensor using optical fibers to route tactile data away from the skin.
card.key_idea: Pairs each mechanical pin with one optical fiber, treating resulting light intensity patterns as images for analytical inference via image moments.
card.evaluation: Tested with various indenters; achieved sub-millimeter localization (RMSE ~0.4mm), linear contact-width estimation, and 96% shape classification accuracy using GMMs.
card.limitation: Performance was tested under controlled laboratory conditions with short fibers; robustness to long routing and repeated bending remains unquantified.

slides.title: Representation-Aligned Tactile Grounding for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation
slides.highlight: This research introduces a Latent Tactile Predictor (LTP) that aligns intermediate action representations with future contact consequences to improve contact-rich manipulation.

card.one_liner: Improves contact-rich robotic manipulation by grounding VLA policies using future tactile prediction at specific intermediate representations.
card.key_idea: Uses linear probes to identify intermediate action-expert features as the optimal interface for a Latent Tactile Predictor (LTP) to supervise contact dynamics.
card.evaluation: Tested on five real-world tasks using SmolVLA and π0 backbones; achieved 74% and 73% average success rates, respectively.

slides.title: MVP-Tac: A Miniaturized Dual-Modal Vision and Photoelastic Tactile Sensor for Robot-Assisted Minimally Invasive Surgery
slides.tldr: DUAL-MODAL VISION AND TACTILE SENSOR FOR MINIMALLY INVASIVE SURGERY
slides.highlight: MVP-Tac integrates reflective photoelastic imaging to provide co-located vision and tactile sensing, enabling tumor palpation and hardness classification without sacrificing visual feedback.

card.one_liner: MVP-Tac is a miniaturized dual-modal sensor providing co-located vision and photoelastic tactile sensing for RMIS.
card.key_idea: Uses a reflective circular polariscope and a semi-transparent membrane to switch between visual navigation and stress-dependent photoelastic imaging for force estimation and hardness classification.
card.evaluation: Validated via force calibration (0-2N), tissue phantoms (97% exposed/92% subdermal tumor classification accuracy), and a simulated colonoscopy with 3D luminal mapping.
card.limitation: VytaFlex elastomer causes slow recovery, hysteresis (9.46%), and reduced sensitivity near the 2N compression limit.

slides.authors: Md Rakibul Islam Prince et al.

slides.title: MIDAS Hand: Modular low-Impedance Direct-drive Anthropomorphic Sensing Hand
slides.highlight: The MIDAS Hand provides a human-scale platform with integrated tactile sensing and low backdrive torque, supporting the human-to-robot data collection and physics-based sensing required for MOSAIC.

card.one_liner: A low-cost, open-source, human-scale dexterous hand featuring directly-driven actuation and integrated multi-axis tactile sensing.
card.key_idea: Combines 13 active DoFs, 3D-printed modular construction, and 283 tactile taxels with low-friction rigid linkages to achieve high backdrivability and human-like thumb opposition.
card.evaluation: Validated via GRASP taxonomy (32/33 types), backdrive torque measurements (~0.02 Nm), payload tests (>9.5 kg), and 5,000+ cycle reliability tests.
card.limitation: Lacks a little finger, limiting some ulnar-side grasps, and tactile sensing is not yet integrated into closed-loop control.

slides.title: Catch, Throw, Repeat: Planning for Human-Robot Partner Juggling
slides.highlight: This work presents a planning and control architecture for synchronized multi-ball juggling between humans and robots, contributing to the study of physical human-robot interaction relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: A real-time planning system enabling a robot to perform synchronized multi-ball partner juggling with humans.
card.key_idea: Integrates predictive ball tracking, state-machine coordination logic, and adaptive online trajectory optimization using a multiple-shooting formulation to catch and throw balls dynamically.
card.evaluation: User study with 8 participants (beginner to expert); achieved 3-ball cascades and 100% success in single-ball trials. Results exceed previous records.
card.limitation: Performance is constrained by timing pressure at high ball counts and lack of explicit spatial coordination to avoid inter-ball collisions.

slides.title: BayesContact: Uncertain Pose Estimation via Visuo-Tactile Proposals and Simulation-based Inference
slides.tldr: VISUO-TACTILE POSE ESTIMATION VIA SIMULATION-BASED INFERENCE
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework for visuo-tactile pose estimation that fuses depth observations with contact evidence, contributing to the multimodal perception goals of HyECHO.

card.one_liner: BayesContact uses simulation-based inference to fuse visuo-tactile data for precise object pose estimation during insertion.
card.key_idea: A Sequential Monte Carlo framework using a graphics renderer for depth likelihoods and a physics simulator for contact likelihoods to maintain a multimodal pose belief.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on five peg-in-hole geometries via simulation and real-robot experiments; improved pose observability and insertion success by 30% over vision-only methods.
card.limitation: Contact-phase updates omit Metropolis-Hastings rejuvenation because each likelihood evaluation requires computationally expensive physics simulations.

slides.title: VTAP Gripper: Synergizing Fingertip Sensing and a Visuo-Tactile Active Palm for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a gripper combining a visuo-tactile active palm with tactile array sensors to achieve robust grasping and fine manipulation. It utilizes a gesture-conditioned retargeting framework for teleoperation, demonstrating success in tasks like syringe reorientation and small object singulation.

card.one_liner: A 13-DOF gripper combining an active bi-modal palm and tactile fingertips for dexterous in-hand manipulation.
card.key_idea: Integrates a visuo-tactile active palm with compliant fingers and a gesture-conditioned retargeting framework to bridge the embodiment gap between human hands and the three-finger structure.
card.evaluation: Tested on YCB objects, syringe reorientation (65% success), object singulation (down to 3mm), and peg-in-hole insertion (70% success) using a UR5e arm.
card.limitation: VR hand-tracking occlusions can cause unintentional grasp release during complex teleoperated motions.
